chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Learning instruments from Johnny; Johnny's composing and arranging
summary: Johnny started Reb on trumpet and saxophone along with drums and wrote his first march at thirteen; Spikes shows a picture of Johnny directing a concert band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: At what point did you start playing saxophone? At what point did you go from drums to saxophone?

Oh, when I started playing drums, that was the beginning. My brother started me right on the rest of them soon as I got the drums, you know. He started me on trumpet and saxophone and I was playing all these other things before he even played the saxophone and trumpet. He had some of these instruments when he took me with him then.
Well, your brother was principally a piano player, but he knew how to teach you all these other instruments? Did he play them, too?
Yeahhh. My brother Johnny, the one that I worked with, when he was thirteen years old, he wrote his first

number, a big...a school band's march. I got it in there somewhere with his picture and everything on it, and he started to writing when he was thirteen--twelve...thirteen years old...composing...arranging and everything. He was a great trumpet player, and a great piano player, and then he had several big bands. Cut it off a minute and I think maybe I can get you one of his pictures...one of...see, right here.
A picture of the Afro-American Concert Band.
Yeah, there he is, directing the band, but this is after he was blind and everything for years and everything.
